verdict.rationale: FireHydrant does offer 'internal status pages' scoped to internal team only, and separate external status pages, but its docs explicitly state internal pages 'do not require auth' and are 'meant for the internal team only and require no setup' — i.e., there's no documented access-control/authentication layer for restricting these pages to specific customer or employee audiences, which is the core of this story. Missing for 10: documented audience-based access control (e.g., SSO-gated or role-based viewer permissions) on internal/private status pages, ability to scope a page to a specific customer segment, and any evidence of granular audience restriction beyond public-vs-internal.
